# Implement block: Referral Reward Card (React Native)

You are adding the "Referral Reward Card" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A "Refer friends" card of clear glass over colored light. A row of friends runs under a fixed lens, with the points they have earned above it, three reward marks in the corner and one button. Press it and the button becomes a comet that the lens ring catches and slings into a rolling counter; tap the friend under the lens and it opens into a capsule with their name and an Invite action.

**Motion.** The row is one Skia canvas driven by Reanimated shared values. Outside the lens avatars are 52 pt, dimmed, and blurred more with every step from the middle (sigma 0, 1.1, 3 pt, eased between); inside it the same row is drawn at 72 pt, so scrolling reads as a magnifier passing over it. A drag follows the finger from where the row is; a flick settles on a friend with a spring (400 ms, damping ratio 0.86) that keeps its velocity and streaks with a horizontal motion blur, while a slow drag stays sharp; a tap brings a friend to the lens without overshoot (380 ms, damping ratio 1). On a referral press the button collapses to a 12 pt dot over 140 ms as its label blurs and fades, with opacity gated by fits(shape) = 1 - clamp((shape - 0.1) / 0.3, 0, 1); the dot launches from the button into one clockwise orbit of the lens and is slung into the points on one path sampled by arc length (1.3 → 0.45 → 1.1 → 0 pt/ms, about 655 ms for a 48 pt-tall footer button), the lens swells 5% at the catch with its ring, ticks and light, the body re-forms on a spring (420 ms, 0.8) starting 120 ms after launch, and the digits start their 520 ms roll 40 ms before landing. A tier sends a second comet from the points to its mark in 440 ms, and the mark fills on a spring as it lands. The card view has no fill or clip. One shader draws the three lamps, page spill, slab and measured button; the white button overlay uses clamp(shape, 0, 1)^4 and is hidden during the comet hand-off. The button radius is max(24, measured height/2) pt, collapsing to 6 pt; both labels reserve even-point width and height before swapping. The light and ripples loop linearly over 14800 ms, independently of autoPlay and continuing after touch; under Reduce Motion phase stands still. The slab's 26 pt bevel bends the field by up to 46 pt, sampling red/green/blue at 1.2/1/0.8 times that shift (one RGB sample below 0.125 pt); transmission is 0.94 times (1 + ripples). Directional highlight strength is 0.10 + 0.64*max(f,0)^2 + 0.26*max(-f,0)^3. The button face is the refracted field times (0.92 - 0.04*press)*(1 + ripples), plus 0.085 - 0.02*press; its bevel and contact shadow contract on press. Stationary per-device-pixel grain both multiplies and adds. Secondary copy is white at 72%, the reward caption 90%, the hint 60%; reward-disc and check-badge gaps use dstOut so the glass shows. Reduce Transparency immediately uses #0C0C0D with a 1 pt white-at-12% inside border and a #1C1C1E to #262628 button with a one-device-pixel white-at-10% border, without surface lamps or grain. The card starts as glass while the iOS setting is read and a failed query leaves its current setting unchanged. Ports without runtime shaders use this plain surface. The complete uniform, lamp, ripple, refraction, compositing and fallback formulas are in catalog/cards/referral-reward-card.md. Haptics: a selection tick per friend passed by hand, a light impact at each catch, a success notification with each reward. With Reduce Motion on, the row moves with a 200 ms ease and no blur, the digits crossfade, and there is no referral collapse, swell or comet; the glass and stationary lamps remain. The capsule uses one peek value: the 84 pt ring opens to the card content width on a 520 ms spring (0.78), closes on a 360 ms spring (1), and reveals the name, status and action from 0.35, 0.42 and 0.5 over 0.4 of peek with opacity, 4 pt blur and 10 pt drift (the action scales from 0.92); Invite collapses its measured action to the same 12 pt dot and waits for a circular ring before the catch. Taps and drags can interrupt it; accessibility activation toggles it, opening is announced, and Reduce Motion keeps a 200 ms shape change with content crossfades only. The comet tail uses reach = min(40, max(t/0.005, 1)) and taper = max(1 - k/reach, 0)^1.3, so it tapers over the length that has left its origin. The open capsule is a darker pane, rgba(4,4,8,0.46). The latest layout stacks the header when card width - 48 < 152*fontScale + 12 + 126, measures the reward comet target from that layout, and uses a 44 pt-high capsule Invite action with a hit target at least 44 pt in both axes; joined friends have no action. Zuzu's key lamp is #FFAE2B while the portrait/lens/comet color stays #FFD966.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
